chapters.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
chapters.tease: Two systems share the cockpit of your mind, and the loud, fast one is almost always flying the plane.

chapters.title: Influence
chapters.tease: Persuasion is not magic. It is six levers, and once you can name them, the strings stop working quite so well.

chapters.title: Predictably Irrational
chapters.tease: Our mistakes are not random. They repeat, they are systematic, and that predictability is both the problem and the way out.

chapters.title: The Righteous Mind
chapters.tease: We reach moral conclusions first and reason our way to them afterwards. The rider thinks it steers; mostly it narrates the elephant.

chapters.title: Mindset
chapters.tease: Whether you think ability is fixed or growable quietly decides how you meet every hard thing for the rest of your life.

chapters.title: Quiet
chapters.tease: In a culture that rewards the loudest voice, the quietest one is often holding the best idea and waiting to be asked.

chapters.title: Stumbling on Happiness
chapters.tease: We are terrible fortune tellers of our own feelings, and the errors are so reliable you can actually plan around them.

chapters.title: Man's Search for Meaning
chapters.tease: Everything can be taken from a person except one thing: the freedom to choose their attitude in any set of circumstances.

chapters.title: The Body Keeps the Score
chapters.tease: Trauma is not just a memory. It is a residue in the body that keeps sounding the alarm long after danger has gone.

chapters.title: Sapiens
chapters.tease: We conquered the planet not with sharper claws but with a stranger power: believing in things that exist only in shared imagination.

chapters.title: The Psychology of Money
chapters.tease: Doing well with money has surprisingly little to do with how smart you are and almost everything to do with how you behave.

chapters.title: The Intelligent Investor
chapters.tease: The market is a moody partner offering daily to buy or sell. Your job is to exploit his moods, not catch them.

chapters.title: Rich Dad Poor Dad
chapters.tease: The rich do not work for money. They buy assets that work for them, and knowing the difference is the whole game.

chapters.title: The Millionaire Next Door
chapters.tease: Most millionaires do not look like millionaires. They look like your frugal neighbour, because that is exactly how they got there.

chapters.title: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
chapters.tease: Almost nobody consistently beats the market, so the evidence says stop trying and simply own all of it, cheaply.

chapters.title: Your Money or Your Life
chapters.tease: Every pound you spend is a piece of your finite life energy traded away, so the real question is whether you got your life's worth.

chapters.title: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
chapters.tease: The man who invented the index fund has one message: costs are the enemy, so own the whole market and hold on.

chapters.title: Thinking in Bets
chapters.tease: A good decision can lead to a bad outcome, and a terrible one can get lucky, so stop judging choices by how they turned out.

chapters.title: Misbehaving
chapters.tease: Economics spent a century pretending humans were rational calculators. This is the story of the rebels who proved we gloriously are not.

chapters.title: Poor Charlie's Almanack
chapters.tease: Munger's method is not a set of tips but a latticework of mental models from every discipline, plus the habit of inverting every problem.

chapters.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
chapters.tease: Why did some peoples end up with guns and steel and others on the receiving end? Not genius or race, but geography.

chapters.title: The Guns of August
chapters.tease: The First World War did not have to happen as it did. It slid into catastrophe on rigid plans, wounded pride and misreadings.

chapters.title: SPQR
chapters.tease: Rome's real achievement was not conquest but an idea, that a person could be a citizen, and Beard asks how we claim to know.

chapters.title: The Silk Roads
chapters.tease: For most of history the centre of the world was not Europe but the crossroads of Asia, where silk, faith, plague and power flowed.
The Americas before Columbus were not an empty wilderness but a crowded, sophisticated world, erased by disease rather than superiority.

chapters.title: The Warmth of Other Suns
chapters.tease: Six million people quietly voted with their feet against a caste system, and in leaving the South they remade a nation.

chapters.title: Postwar
chapters.tease: How does a continent that has just destroyed itself rebuild, divide and slowly stitch itself back toward unity?

chapters.title: The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich
chapters.tease: A modern democracy dismantled itself from within, and a journalist who watched it happen wrote down exactly how.

chapters.title: A People's History of the United States
chapters.tease: History is usually written by the winners. Zinn tells it from below, through the people who paid for it.

chapters.title: The Origins of Totalitarianism
chapters.tease: Arendt dissects how movements persuade millions to abandon reality itself, and warns that the conditions never fully disappear.

chapters.title: A Brief History of Time
chapters.tease: Hawking set out to explain the whole universe, its birth, its black holes and the shape of time, to people who never solve equations.

chapters.title: The Selfish Gene
chapters.tease: Look at evolution from the gene's point of view and everything flips: we are vehicles that genes build to carry themselves forward.

chapters.title: Cosmos
chapters.tease: Sagan wanted us to feel our true place in the universe, a pale blue dot in an ocean of stars, with science as a candle.

chapters.title: The Gene
chapters.tease: The story of heredity is a story about ourselves, and we have just moved from reading the code of life to rewriting it.

chapters.title: The Emperor of All Maladies
chapters.tease: Cancer is not one disease but a shape shifting adversary, and this is the four thousand year biography of our war against it.

chapters.title: Silent Spring
chapters.tease: One careful scientist with evidence and clear prose proved a nation was poisoning itself, and launched the modern environmental movement.

chapters.title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
chapters.tease: The most important cells in modern medicine were taken from a poor Black woman without her knowledge, and her family never saw a penny.

chapters.title: Entangled Life
chapters.tease: Beneath your feet runs a kingdom we barely notice, fungi, which link forests, digest rock and blur the line between one life and many.

chapters.title: The Order of Time
chapters.tease: Everything you feel about time, that it flows, that there is a universal now, that the past is fixed, may be a local illusion.

chapters.title: The Beginning of Infinity
chapters.tease: Deutsch makes an audacious claim: good explanations have no natural limit, so knowledge and human progress can grow without end.

chapters.title: Atomic Habits
chapters.tease: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems, built one tiny action at a time.

chapters.title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
chapters.tease: Covey's framework is a staircase, from depending on others, to standing alone, to realising the biggest things are done together.

chapters.title: Deep Work
chapters.tease: Undistracted concentration is becoming rare at exactly the moment it is becoming the most valuable skill in the economy.

chapters.title: Getting Things Done
chapters.tease: Your mind is for having ideas, not holding them, and much of your anxiety is open loops it keeps rehearsing.

chapters.title: Grit
chapters.tease: Talent counts once but effort counts twice, and the people who go furthest are rarely the most gifted, just the least willing to quit.

chapters.title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
chapters.tease: You have a limited supply of things to care about, and most people spend it on nonsense. The art is in the allocation.

chapters.title: Daring Greatly
chapters.tease: Vulnerability is not weakness. It is the truest measure of courage, and the birthplace of love, belonging and creativity.

chapters.title: Flow
chapters.tease: The best moments of a life are not passive ones but those spent stretched doing something difficult and worthwhile, as time disappears.

chapters.title: Essentialism
chapters.tease: If you do not prioritise your life, someone else will, and the disciplined pursuit of less is how your yes lands where it counts.

chapters.title: The War of Art
chapters.tease: Every creator's enemy has a name, Resistance, and it wakes up with you every morning determined to keep you from your work.

chapters.title: Good to Great
chapters.tease: Great companies were not built by charismatic saviours or big bangs, but by disciplined people pushing a flywheel until momentum took over.

chapters.title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
chapters.tease: There is no recipe for the moments that define a company, only the honesty of someone who has survived them.

chapters.title: Start with Why
chapters.tease: People do not buy what you do, they buy why you do it, and inspiring leaders communicate from the inside of the circle out.

chapters.title: The Lean Startup
chapters.tease: A startup is not a small big company. It is a machine for learning what to build, and learning speed is its only real advantage.

chapters.title: High Output Management
chapters.tease: A manager's output is not their own work but their team's, and everyone they influence, which makes leverage the heart of the job.

chapters.title: Never Split the Difference
chapters.tease: Negotiation is not a battle of arguments but an act of discovery, and the strongest tool is making the other side feel understood.

chapters.title: Extreme Ownership
chapters.tease: The leader owns everything in their world, every failure, every excuse, and that total accountability turns out to be a superpower.

chapters.title: Measure What Matters
chapters.tease: Ideas are easy and execution is everything, and OKRs are the simple, brutal system that keeps an organisation honest.

chapters.title: Multipliers
chapters.tease: Some leaders make everyone around them smarter and some make everyone smaller, and the diminishers usually have no idea.

chapters.title: Thinking in Systems
chapters.tease: The world is a web of stocks, flows and feedback loops, and until you see that structure, you will keep fixing symptoms.

chapters.title: The New Jim Crow
chapters.tease: Alexander argues mass incarceration does not merely contain racial injustice. It works as a racial caste system rebuilt in colourblind language.

chapters.title: Why Nations Fail
chapters.tease: Nations are not poor because of geography or culture, the authors argue, but because their institutions are built to extract rather than include.

chapters.title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
chapters.tease: Piketty's centuries of data point to an uncomfortable law: when returns on capital outpace growth, wealth concentrates, automatically.

chapters.title: The Better Angels of Our Nature
chapters.tease: Against every instinct the news sharpens, Pinker uses centuries of data to argue that war, murder and cruelty have declined dramatically.

chapters.title: Evicted
chapters.tease: Desmond lived alongside eight Milwaukee families to show a brutal inversion: losing your home is not just a result of poverty, but a cause.

chapters.title: Between the World and Me
chapters.tease: Written as a letter to his teenage son, Coates asks what it means to live in a country built on the destruction of Black bodies.

chapters.title: Bowling Alone
chapters.tease: Americans did not stop bowling. They stopped bowling in leagues, and that quiet collapse of clubs and congregations has real costs.

chapters.title: The Color of Law
chapters.tease: American segregation was not an accident of private prejudice. Rothstein shows it was engineered street by street by government policy.

chapters.title: Nickel and Dimed
chapters.tease: Ehrenreich went undercover in low wage jobs to answer a simple question: can you actually live on that pay? The answer is no.

chapters.title: The Wretched of the Earth
chapters.tease: Written as empires fell, Fanon's incendiary classic dissects colonialism from the inside: what it does to lands, and to minds.

chapters.title: The Innovator's Dilemma
chapters.tease: Great companies fail not despite doing everything right, but because of it, while a cheap little rival quietly eats them.

chapters.title: Superintelligence
chapters.tease: If machine intelligence ever exceeds ours, Bostrom argues, it may be history's most important event, and we may get one chance to get it right.

chapters.title: The Shallows
chapters.tease: The internet is not just changing what we read. It is rewiring how we think, trading the deep mind of the book for the feed.

chapters.title: The Age of Surveillance Capitalism
chapters.tease: Zuboff names a new economic order where your behaviour is raw material, harvested free and refined into predictions sold to whoever wants to steer you.

chapters.title: Weapons of Math Destruction
chapters.tease: The algorithms deciding who is hired, insured and sentenced are often opaque, unaccountable and biased: objectivity worn as a costume.

chapters.title: Life 3.0
chapters.tease: Life one evolved, life two learned culture, and life three could redesign itself. Tegmark asks what future we want before it arrives.

chapters.title: The Master Algorithm
chapters.tease: Five tribes of machine learning, each with its own philosophy of knowledge, are racing toward one algorithm that could learn anything.

chapters.title: Hackers
chapters.tease: Before the internet had users it had believers, and Levy captures the ethic that built the digital world: access, openness and code.

chapters.title: The Alignment Problem
chapters.tease: Teaching machines to want what we actually want, not what we said or measured, may be the deepest problem in the field.

chapters.title: Genesis
chapters.tease: When machines out think us where we cannot check their work, what happens to human judgement, and to power?

chapters.title: Why We Sleep
chapters.tease: Sleep is not the absence of activity but the most powerful thing you do all day, and skimping on it quietly sabotages everything.

chapters.title: Breath
chapters.tease: We take twenty five thousand breaths a day and most of us do it badly. Relearning this automatic act can transform health.

chapters.title: How Not to Die
chapters.tease: Most diseases that kill us are, to a large degree, choices we make three times a day, and Greger gathers the evidence on prevention.

chapters.title: The Blue Zones
chapters.tease: In a few places around the world people routinely reach a hundred in good health, and the secret is a shared way of living.

chapters.title: Spark
chapters.tease: Exercise is not just for the body. Ratey shows it is the most powerful tool we have for the brain.

chapters.title: Outlive
chapters.tease: Attia wants to change medicine's goal from adding years to your life to adding life to your years, starting decades early.

chapters.title: The Obesity Code
chapters.tease: For decades we treated weight as simple arithmetic. Fung argues the driver is hormonal, and when you eat may matter as much as how much.

chapters.title: When Breath Becomes Air
chapters.tease: A neurosurgeon near the end of his training is diagnosed with terminal cancer, and asks what makes a life worth living as it ends.

chapters.title: Being Mortal
chapters.tease: Modern medicine is superb at fighting death and poor at helping people live well while dying. Gawande asks what we have lost.

chapters.title: The Emperor's New Drugs
chapters.tease: Kirsch reanalysed the antidepressant trials, unpublished ones included, and claimed the drugs beat placebo by far less than we were told.

chapters.title: Meditations
chapters.tease: The most powerful man in the world kept a private notebook to stay humble, just and calm. It was never meant for you.

chapters.title: Letters from a Stoic
chapters.tease: Seneca's letters to a young friend read as if written last week: warm, practical advice on spending time, the one currency you cannot earn back.

chapters.title: The Tao Te Ching
chapters.tease: In eighty one short verses from twenty five centuries ago, Lao Tzu maps a strange route to power: yielding, softness and doing by not doing.

chapters.title: The Denial of Death
chapters.tease: Becker argues nearly everything humans build, religion, empire, art, ambition, is a defence against the one fact we cannot face: we die.

chapters.title: The Wisdom of Insecurity
chapters.tease: Watts diagnoses the modern ache: our craving for security and certainty is the very thing making us anxious.

chapters.title: Tao of Pooh
chapters.tease: Hoff explains Taoism through Winnie the Pooh, and a bear of very little brain turns out to be the wisest one in the wood.

chapters.title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
chapters.tease: A father and son ride across America while the narrator hunts his own former self, and the deepest question: what do we mean by Quality?

chapters.title: The Prophet
chapters.tease: As a beloved prophet prepares to sail home, people ask him about love, work, children and grief, and his answers are still read today.

chapters.title: The Myth of Sisyphus
chapters.tease: Camus asks whether life is worth living, and answers a universe without built in meaning not with despair, but with revolt.

chapters.title: How to Live
chapters.tease: Bakewell frames Montaigne's life as twenty answers to one question, how to live, from the man who more or less invented the essay.
